title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. The preregistered benign-control and its false-positive-blocking estimand were not executed. We reconcile preregistration language versus the formal estimand, disclose a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, promising automation gains for network operations (NetOps). Yet produced outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can exacerbate these risks [1–4]. Prior prototypes indicate that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded repair reduces observable errors, but many evaluations rely on surface or token-match metrics that do not measure deployability or validator acceptance [3,5,6].

Research question. How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a precise, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics that isolates post-generation safeguards; (3) confirmatory quantitative results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in deterministic-validator acceptance on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (4) an explicit reconciliation of preregistration wording with the formal estimand and disclosure of a protocol deviation that affects sampling determinism.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber) provide semantics-focused checks (reachability, isolation, rule precedence) and are natural deployment gates for generated configurations [7–9]. LLM-for-NetOps studies (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench, zero-touch proposals) report that model-only generation often yields syntactic and higher-level semantic errors (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches) and argue for validator-centered evaluation metrics [3,5,10]. Generate–validate–repair architectures—where an LLM produces a draft, a verifier checks it, and feedback is used to repair—have shown promise in prototype settings but depend on precise verifier diagnostics and constrained repair policies [11,12]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in LLM-integrated operational pipelines [13]. Surveys call for operationally grounded benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than token overlap alone [4]. This study situates itself against those gaps by preregistering a validator-acceptance estimand and executing an artifact-backed paired test that isolates post-generation safeguards.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256 archived). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepts the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729).

Design and task bank. The confirmatory paired design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired Baseline–Guarded). Synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU/VLAN updates, and required sequencing patterns (shutdown–change–restore). The adversary applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates; generation seeds and task payloads were archived. Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator; no production operator logs or private data were used.

Model, validator, and pipeline semantics. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Generation semantics were preregistered as shared_initial_candidate: a single LLM candidate was produced per intent pair and reused by both conditions. The guarded branch applied template-based input sanitization prior to determinstic gating; policy permitted at-most-one automated repair LLM call per pair. Repair calls and verifier diagnostics were logged in archived artifacts. The archived model configuration records that sampling temperature was unset at runtime (a protocol deviation disclosed below).

Missingness, exclusions, and analysis plan. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar) on complete pairs; sensitivity analyses treat excluded pairs conservatively as failures. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the associated false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; this omission is reported here and limits empirical conclusions about false-positive blocking (see Results and Discussion).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a pair only when both paired runs failed technically) 141 complete pairs entered the primary confirmatory analysis (complete_pairs = 141; both_missing_pairs = 9).

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Baseline accepted final candidates for deployment in 135/141 complete pairs (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383). Guarded accepted in 141/141 complete pairs (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table gives n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test on these paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. A 95% bootstrap percentile confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric results and test parameters are archived in the run's analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable to permitted repair-stage activity: stage_counts recorded repair = 6 and provider-call accounting links those repairs to the discordant episodes. For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate was identical across conditions; the guarded pipeline applied sanitizer and, where permitted, a single automated repair that produced a final candidate the validator accepted. Representative scoring artifacts show repair_applied flags for those episodes. Thus the guarded increase in validator acceptance in these discordant cases resulted from sanitizer normalization and/or a single automatic repair that converted an initially rejected draft into a validator-accepted candidate.

Missingness sensitivity. As a conservative sensitivity check (not the preregistered primary analysis), treating the nine excluded both-failure pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; direction of the observed paired difference remains unchanged under this conservative assumption.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported. This omission constrains operational claims about the guarded pipeline's propensity to block benign operator intents.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and alignment with preregistration. The preregistration's natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success. The formal estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment; an observed increase in validator acceptance can result from repairs that recover otherwise-rejectable but benign drafts. Our findings—an absolute paired increase ≈ 4.255 percentage points driven by six discordant repairs—therefore reflect improved validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline, not a demonstrated decrease in attacker success under an attacker-centric definition. Practitioners should avoid conflating validator acceptance with attacker remediation unless an independent semantic-safety oracle is used.

Operational implications and co-design. Within this synthetic setting, sanitizer-plus-bounded-repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. However, this operational benefit requires co-design: (1) gating policies must limit repair scope to avoid masking adversarial manipulations; (2) verifier expressiveness must cover the safety properties of interest; and (3) benign-control measurements are necessary to quantify false-positive blocking. The absent benign-control in this run prevents empirical statements about false-positive blocking and is therefore a priority for follow-up.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; exclusions followed the preregistered rule. Construct validity: validator acceptance is a partial proxy for deployability and does not capture all protocol-level or runtime dynamics. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini), single validator implementation, and synthetic task bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production conditions. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical significance does not imply large operational impact.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (protocol deviation). To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per pair). For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting sampling to a fixed value (e.g., temperature = 0) and re-running the archived manifest under identical provider semantics; the run's execution and analysis artifacts record provider-call accounting and per-episode traces that enable artifact-grounded verification.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank, template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics attribute the observed discordant conversions to permitted repairs that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not, by itself, demonstrate reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Limitations—synthetic scope, single model/validator, absent benign-control, and a protocol deviation (unset temperature)—constrain operational generalization. Follow-up work should execute the preregistered benign-control, add an independent semantic-safety oracle for attacker-centric estimands, diversify models and validators, and fix sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and provided pre-lock constraints; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared artifacts and tools: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; preregistration id = cand-2026-03 (archived preregistration SHA available). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature; this is disclosed because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting confirms the actual call pattern. The archive contains the execution and analysis manifests and all per-episode traces referenced in Methods and Results. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
